newsitem.title: USA: Ex-Astra executive pleads guilty to tax charge.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Astra executive pleads guilty to tax charge.

text.p: The former senior vice president of Astra U.S.A., Inc, a subsidiary of the Swedish pharmaceutical giant Astra Ab, pleaded guilty on Thursday to charges that he filed a falsified a state income tax return, prosecutors said.

Stefan Solvell, 43, of Wellsley, Massachusetts plead guilty in Suffolk Superior Court to one count of filing a false state income tax return. Judge Vieri Volterra gave him a two-year suspended prison sentence, with two years of probation and ordered him to pay a $5,000 fine.
Solvell primarily worked as second in command at the Westborough, Massachusetts-based Astra U.S.A. until he left the company in 1995.

He was recruited and hired by Lars Bildman, former Astra U.S.A. president and chief executive officer, who is facing charges that he allegedly defrauded the firm out of more than $1 million and filed false federal and state tax returns.
